newsitem.title: USA: U.S. approves $20 billion BT/MCI deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. approves $20 billion BT/MCI deal.

text.p: The United States on Monday gave British Telecommunications PLC permission to acquire the American long distance company MCI, but put some conditons on the $20 billion deal.

The Justice Department will require some changes in a 1994 consent decree permitting British Telecom to buy 20 percent of MCI. "We need to make certain changes to the consent decree and extend it to ensure that U.S. consumers continue to enjoy the lower prices and better service associated with competition on international routes," said Joel Klein, acting assistant attorney general in charge of the antitrust division.
The deal had been approved in May by European antitrust regulators, but they required MCI to provide space for competitors on its submarine cables.
"We're building on the work we did before and building on the work" of the Europeans, said Larry Fullerton, deputy assistant attorney general.
The Justice Department's earlier consent decree was set to expire in 1999, but will now be extended to 2004.

In addition, the Justice Department requires that the new, combined company -- to be known as Concert Plc -- cannot disclose to its MCI division competitively sensitive information it has obtained from other U.S. carriers.
